## Current OPALX Field Maps {#opalx-field-maps}

OPALX provides the seven field-map formats below. Availability describes the
current supported scope: ✅ **Available**, 🟡 **Partially available** (a subset
of the format or its options), and ⚪ **Unavailable**.

| Format | Availability now | Current scope |
|---|---|---|
| `AstraDynamic` | ✅ Available | 1D on-axis RF field map for standing-wave `RFCAVITY` and `TRAVELINGWAVE`; for `TRAVELINGWAVE`, the source map must start at `z=0 m` |
| `AstraMagnetoStatic` | ✅ Available | 1D on-axis static magnetic field map with Fourier reconstruction. |
| `3DDynamic` | ✅ Available | 3D Cartesian RF field map for standing-wave `RFCAVITY`; automatic phase estimation requires the map to cover the local axis `x=y=0`. |
| `2DMagnetoStatic` | 🟡 Partially available | Normalized magnetic maps with radial origin `r=0`; explicit `TRUE`/`FALSE` normalization flags currently do not work; omit the flag to use automatic normalization |
| `2DDynamic` | 🟡 Partially available | Normalized RF maps with radial origin `r=0`; use the documented `XZ`/`ZX` columns; explicit `TRUE`/`FALSE` normalization flags currently do not work; omit the flag to use automatic normalization |
| G4beamline `cylinder` | 🟡 Partially available | `Bz`/`Br` block format; electric fields, `Bphi`, `data` and symmetry sections are unavailable |
| G4beamline `grid` | 🟡 Partially available | Six- or nine-column `data` format; `points`, symmetry sections and `ZREVERSE` are unavailable |

Future support for the missing options and formats is **unconfirmed**. The
historical OPAL descriptions below, including material formerly marked
planned, do not establish a current OPALX implementation commitment.

The descriptor is read from the beginning of the first non-comment record.
Comments begin with `#`. G4beamline maps have no descriptor; OPALX recognizes
them by their first keyword, an optional `param` line followed by `cylinder` or
`grid`. The file extension does not matter.

### Element compatibility {#opalx-map-element-compatibility}

Reader availability does not mean that every element accepts that format.

| Element/model | Accepted maps |
|---|---|
| [`FIELDMAP`](../../elements.qmd#fieldmap) | `2DMagnetoStatic`, `AstraMagnetoStatic`, G4beamline `cylinder` and `grid`; dynamic maps are rejected |
| [`SOLENOID`](../../elements.qmd#solenoid) | `2DMagnetoStatic`, `AstraMagnetoStatic`, G4beamline `cylinder` and magnetic-only `grid` maps; use `FIELDMAP` for maps containing electric fields |
| [`RFCAVITY`, `TYPE="STANDING"`](../../elements.qmd#rfcavity) | `AstraDynamic`, `2DDynamic`, `3DDynamic` |
| [`RFCAVITY`, `TYPE="IDEAL"`](../../elements.qmd#rfcavity-ideal) | no field map; `FMAPFN` is rejected |
| [`TRAVELINGWAVE`](../../elements.qmd#travelingwave) | `AstraDynamic`; the source map must begin at `z=0` |

`CYCLOTRONSECTOR` and `RFCAVITY, TYPE="SINGLEGAP"` use separate loaders for
sector fields and voltage profiles. See the
[cyclotron guide](../../cyclotron.qmd) for their configuration.

⚪ The `FAST` accelerated field-map mode is currently unavailable; changing
`FAST` does not select a different field evaluation mode. Future support is
unconfirmed. For static-map placement and the independent `BSCALE` and `ESCALE`
multipliers, see the [`FIELDMAP` reference](../../elements.qmd#fieldmap).

### `AstraDynamic` and `AstraMagnetoStatic` {#opalx-astra-field-maps}

The ASTRA readers spline-resample non-equidistant on-axis data onto an
equidistant grid, mirror the profile periodically, and construct a truncated
Fourier representation for off-axis field evaluation. The number of retained
Fourier modes specified in the header controls the reconstruction.

The first line is `AstraDynamic N_Fourier [TRUE|FALSE]` or
`AstraMagnetoStatic N_Fourier [TRUE|FALSE]`. `AstraDynamic` then reads a frequency
in MHz and `(z [m], Ez [MV/m])` records; `AstraMagnetoStatic` reads
`(z [m], Bz [T])` records immediately after its header. The optional flag defaults
to `TRUE` and controls normalization of the input profile to a peak absolute
on-axis field of 1 MV/m or 1 T, respectively. Supply increasing axial samples
and a nonzero on-axis field;
both readers reject a zero peak even with normalization disabled. Neither
reader provides a `FAST` variant.

### `2DMagnetoStatic` {#opalx-2d-magnetostatic}

The header declares `XZ` or `ZX` ordering. Axis bounds are in cm, and each
count is the number of intervals: a count of `N` gives `N+1` grid points.
Samples contain `Bz Br` in `XZ` order or `Br Bz` in `ZX` order, in tesla.
Data advance fastest in `z` for `XZ` ordering and in `r` for `ZX` ordering.
The reader uses bilinear interpolation and normalizes the on-axis longitudinal
field to a peak magnitude of 1 T.

```text
2DMagnetoStatic XZ
z_begin_cm z_end_cm Nz_intervals
0 r_end_cm Nr_intervals
Bz Br
...
```

For `ZX`, put the radial bounds/count first and the longitudinal bounds/count
second. Radial grids must start at zero; nonzero radial origins are currently
unsupported.

### `2DDynamic` {#opalx-2d-dynamic}

This RF format uses axis bounds in cm and interval counts, giving
`(Nz_intervals+1)(Nr_intervals+1)` samples. The frequency in MHz appears between
the two axis records for both orderings. Use a radial grid starting at zero.

```text
2DDynamic XZ
z_begin_cm z_end_cm Nz_intervals
frequency_MHz
0 r_end_cm Nr_intervals
Ez Er unused Hphi
...
```

For `ZX`, the radial bounds/count come first and the longitudinal bounds/count
come after the frequency. The current reader consumes data as follows:

| Ordering | Data columns |
|---|---|
| `XZ` | `Ez Er unused Hphi` |
| `ZX` | `Er Ez Hphi unused` |

Data advance fastest in `z` for `XZ` ordering and in `r` for `ZX` ordering.

Electric components are in MV/m and `Hphi` is in A/m. Use the column order for
the selected orientation when preparing or converting a map.

Normalization uses the maximum absolute `Ez` over the entire grid, rather than
only the axis. The resulting peak absolute `Ez` is 1 MV/m. `Hphi` is converted to magnetic
flux density with the same normalization factor and the vacuum permeability
$\mu_0$.

🟡 **Normalization options:** use a two-token header, such as
`2DDynamic XZ`. Explicit `TRUE`/`FALSE` normalization flags currently do not work
for `2DMagnetoStatic` and `2DDynamic`; omit the flag to use automatic
normalization. The ASTRA and
`3DDynamic` normalization flags are available. Future availability of the
missing 2D options is unconfirmed.

### `3DDynamic` {#opalx-3d-dynamic}

`3DDynamic` supplies a Cartesian RF map for mapped standing-wave `RFCAVITY`.
Its complete layout is:

```text
3DDynamic [TRUE|FALSE]
frequency_MHz
x_begin_cm x_end_cm Nx_intervals
y_begin_cm y_end_cm Ny_intervals
z_begin_cm z_end_cm Nz_intervals
Ex Ey Ez Hx Hy Hz
...
```

Each interval count `N` gives `N+1` points. The z index changes fastest,
followed by y and x. Electric components are in MV/m; magnetic-field-strength
components are in A/m and are converted to magnetic flux density using
$\mu_0$. The reader uses trilinear interpolation.

By default, all six components are divided by the maximum absolute on-axis
`Ez` sampled at `x=y=0`. Use `3DDynamic FALSE` when the map does not contain that
axis or has zero on-axis `Ez`. With `FALSE`, physical field values retain their
input scale before the element amplitude is applied. Nonfinite field records
are rejected regardless of the flag. Disabling normalization does not remove
the on-axis requirement of automatic phase estimation; an off-axis-only map
cannot supply that estimate.

Frequency must be finite and nonnegative. Bounds must be finite and strictly
increasing, with at least one interval per axis. Every field component must be
finite, and data after the last expected grid point are rejected.

Mapped standing-wave `RFCAVITY` supplies the RF time dependence: electric
amplitudes multiply $\cos(\omega t+\phi)$ and magnetic amplitudes multiply
$-\sin(\omega t+\phi)$. Here $t$ is in seconds, $\omega$ in rad/s and
$\phi$ in radians; the element also supplies its amplitude and error settings.

### G4beamline maps {#opalx-g4bl-field-maps}

OPALX reads the `cylinder` and `grid` formats written by G4beamline. Positions
are in mm, magnetic fields in tesla, and electric fields in MV/m. Neither reader
normalizes to a field peak. With `BSCALE=1` and `ESCALE=1`, a
[`FIELDMAP`](../../elements.qmd#fieldmap) element preserves the map's field scale
after applying any `param` factors.

An optional first line `param` scales the stored values the same way
G4beamline does. Magnetic values are multiplied by `normB/current` and electric
values by `normE/gradient`. Each key defaults to `1`. `current=0` is rejected,
and so is `gradient=0` in a `grid` map. The `current=` and `gradient=` that
G4beamline gives where it places a map correspond to `BSCALE` and `ESCALE` on
the `FIELDMAP` element.

Symmetry sections (`extendX`, `extendY`, `extendZ`, ...) are rejected by both
readers.

`ZREVERSE` is supported only for a `cylinder` map. The same map filename cannot
be loaded with opposite `ZREVERSE` settings at the same time; use separate files
if both orientations are needed.

#### `cylinder` maps {#opalx-g4bl-cylinder}

A `cylinder` map holds an axially symmetric magnetic field on an r-z grid:

```text
param normB=1. current=1.
cylinder Z0=-1500.0000 nZ=301 dZ=10.0000 nR=51 dR=10.0000
Bz
<nZ rows of nR values>
Br
<nZ rows of nR values>
```

The `cylinder` line gives the first z (`Z0`), the number of points and the
spacing in z (`nZ`, `dZ`), and the same in r (`nR`, `dR`). Each count must be
at least 2. r always starts at 0. `X0`, `Y0`, and `tolerance` are accepted and
ignored. A `Bz` block follows, and optionally a `Br` block; a missing `Br` block
means $B_r=0$. In each block a row is one z point and a column one r point,
with column 0 on the axis. `Er`, `Ez`, and `Bphi` blocks and the one-point-per-row
`data` form are rejected.

The field is interpolated bilinearly in r and z, as for `2DMagnetoStatic`.
`ZREVERSE` mirrors the map in z and negates $B_z$; $B_r$ is unchanged.

#### `grid` maps {#opalx-g4bl-grid}

A `grid` map holds a field on a cartesian grid, one point per row:

```text
param current=1.
grid X0=-200.0000 Y0=-120.0000 Z0=-1380.0000 nX=60 nY=25 nZ=553 dX=10.0000 dY=10.0000 dZ=5.0000
data
-2.0000e+02 -1.2000e+02 -1.3800e+03 6.2742e-05 3.7624e-04 -1.6298e-04
-2.0000e+02 -1.2000e+02 -1.3750e+03 3.7771e-05 3.3956e-04 9.2075e-05
...
```

The `grid` line gives the first point (`X0`, `Y0`, `Z0`), the number of points
(`nX`, `nY`, `nZ`, each at least 2), and the spacing (`dX`, `dY`, `dZ`). Each
row after `data` holds `x y z Bx By Bz`, or nine values
`x y z Bx By Bz Ex Ey Ez`. Rows are placed by their own coordinates, so their
order does not matter. A row more than a quarter of a spacing off the grid, a
row that repeats a point, and a point with no row are all errors. A `points`
section in place of `data` is rejected, and so is `ZREVERSE`.

The field is interpolated trilinearly. Storage for the electric field is
allocated only when a nonzero electric value appears, so nine-column maps whose
electric columns are all zero cost no more than six-column maps.

#### Memory use {#opalx-g4bl-grid-memory}

A `grid` map takes 24 bytes per grid point for the magnetic field, and another
24 bytes per point if it holds a nonzero electric field. The
$60\times25\times553$ map above takes about 20 MB. Every MPI rank holds its own
copy, and GPU builds keep one copy in CPU memory and one in GPU memory.

If memory runs out while a map is loaded, OPALX stops with a message that names
the map. On Linux the operating system may instead accept the request and end
the job without a message once the memory is filled. To reduce the memory
needed, use a coarser grid or a smaller box, or run fewer MPI ranks per node.

### Recognized but unsupported headers {#opalx-unsupported-field-map-headers}

The following additional or legacy formats are unavailable in current OPALX.
A recognized header alone does not make a format usable.

| Format or family | Availability now | Future support |
|---|---|---|
| Legacy `1DDynamic`, `1DMagnetoStatic`, `1DProfile1`, `1DElectroStatic` | ⚪ Unavailable | Unconfirmed |
| `2DElectroStatic` | ⚪ Unavailable | Unconfirmed |
| Legacy `3DMagnetoStatic` (including Extended) and `3DElectroStatic` | ⚪ Unavailable | Unconfirmed |
| H5hut/HDF5 field blocks | ⚪ Unavailable | Unconfirmed |
| `AstraElectroStatic` | ⚪ Unavailable | Unconfirmed |
| Built-in `1DPROFILE1-DEFAULT` profile | ⚪ Unavailable | Unconfirmed |

Recognition is not support: these formats are unavailable in the
currently audited OPALX source tree.

Missing files, unavailable formats and malformed records are rejected with an
error. The error handling described in the historical OPAL section applies to
that historical version.

## Introduction

This appendix documents the field-map types accepted by `OPAL-T`. The legacy
implementation supports several one-, two-, and three-dimensional field-map
formats that originated from different external codes and accelerator
applications.

The original manual groups them into three families:

1. 2D and 3D sampled field maps with interpolation on a grid
2. 1D on-axis profiles reconstructed off axis from a truncated Fourier series
3. Enge-function fringe-field models for selected bend magnets

In all cases, electric maps are normalized to a peak on-axis longitudinal field
of `1 MV/m` and magnetic maps to a peak on-axis longitudinal field of `1 T`,
unless the map type is explicitly documented as an exception.

## Comments in Field Maps

Comments are introduced by `#` and extend to the end of the line. They are
accepted:

- at the beginning of the file
- between data lines
- at the end of a complete data record

They must not split a record that is expected to stay on one line. A valid
example is:

```text
# This is a valid comment
1DMagnetoStatic 40 # This is also valid
-60.0 60.0 9999
# and this is valid too
0.0 2.0 199
```

A broken example is:

```text
1DMagnetoStatic # invalid split record
40
-60.0 60.0 # invalid inline split # 9999
0.0 2.0 199
```

## Normalization

ASCII field maps are normalized with the maximum absolute value of the
longitudinal on-axis field. The documented exception is `1DProfile1`. This
normalization can be disabled by appending `FALSE` to the first line of the
field map.

## Field-Map Warnings and Errors

If `OPAL-T` encounters a parsing error, it disables the corresponding element,
emits a warning, and continues the simulation. The main warning categories are:

- too few lines compared with the header counts
- too many lines compared with the header counts
- wrong number or type of values on a given line
- file not found
- unrecognized field-map descriptor
- too few Fourier coefficients for a 1D field reconstruction

For one-dimensional maps the reconstruction quality is checked with the legacy
criteria

$$
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^N (F_{z,i} - \tilde F_{z,i})^2}{\sum_{i=1}^N F_{z,i}^2} \le 10^{-2},
$$ {#eq-fieldmaps-rms-ratio}

and

$$
\frac{\max_i |F_{z,i} - \tilde F_{z,i}|}{\max_i |F_{z,i}|} \le 10^{-2},
$$ {#eq-fieldmaps-max-ratio}

where `F_z` is the sampled field from the file and `\tilde F_z` is the field
reconstructed after low-pass filtering.

## Types and Format

The legacy appendix lists both implemented and planned descriptors.

### Implemented families

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1DMagnetoStatic` | one-dimensional static magnetic field |
| `AstraMagnetoStatic` | ASTRA magnetic field format with non-equidistant sampling |
| `1DDynamic` | one-dimensional time-dependent RF field |
| `AstraDynamic` | ASTRA dynamic field format |
| `1DProfile1` | Enge-like bend fringe profile |
| `2DElectroStatic` | two-dimensional electrostatic field |
| `2DMagnetoStatic` | two-dimensional static magnetic field |
| `2DDynamic` | two-dimensional dynamic field |
| `3DMagnetoStatic` | three-dimensional static magnetic field |
| `3DMagnetoStatic_Extended` | mid-plane magnetic field extended to 3D |
| `3DDynamic` | three-dimensional dynamic field |

### Planned but not implemented in the historical appendix

| Type | Note |
|---|---|
| `1DElectroStatic` | not implemented; old workaround was `1DDynamic` with very low frequency |
| `3DElectroStatic` | not implemented |

## Field-Map Orientation

Two- and three-dimensional maps carry an orientation string in the header.

For 2D maps:

- `XZ`: primary direction in `z`, secondary in `r`
- `ZX`: primary direction in `r`, secondary in `z`

For 3D maps:

- `XYZ`: primary direction in `z`, secondary in `y`, tertiary in `x`

The primary index increases fastest and the tertiary index slowest.
Accordingly, the first field component column corresponds to the primary
axis-order interpretation. For 2D dynamic maps in `XZ` orientation the four data
columns are:

- `Ez`
- `Er`
- `|E|` (unused by the legacy code)
- `Hphi`

In the alternative 2D orientation, the first two columns are interchanged while
the third and fourth are unchanged.

![Axis-ordering conventions for the legacy field-map orientation rules.](figures/order.png){#fig-fieldmaps-order width="60%"}

## `FAST` Attribute for 1D Field Maps

For some 1D field maps, the boolean attribute `FAST` can be used to speed up
field evaluation. When `FAST = TRUE`, `OPAL-T` generates an internal 2D field
map and then uses bilinear interpolation rather than the slower Fourier-series
technique.

This is faster, but the legacy appendix warns that it can introduce numerical
noise if the generated 2D grid is too coarse.

![Example of field noise caused by insufficient one-dimensional reconstruction.](figures/fieldnoise_example.png){#fig-fieldmaps-noise width="80%"}

## `1DMagnetoStatic`

A `1DMagnetoStatic` map stores one-dimensional static magnetic data on axis. An
example header from the appendix is:

```text
1DMagnetoStatic 40
-60.0 60.0 9999
0.0 2.0 199
```

This describes a map with `10000` longitudinal points (`9999` spacings) from
`-60 cm` to `60 cm` relative to `ELEMEDGE`. The field is normalized so that
`max(|B_on axis|) = 1 T`. The code computes `Nz/2` complex Fourier
coefficients and retains only `N_Fourier` during tracking.

If `FAST = TRUE`, the third line defines the radial range of an internally
generated 2D map. In the example, that is `0 cm` to `2 cm` with `200` radial
values.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `1DMagnetoStatic N_Fourier [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| 2 | `z_start z_end Nz` in cm |
| 3 | `r_start r_end Nr` in cm |
| remaining lines | `Bz` samples in tesla |

## `AstraMagnetoStatic`

This format accepts non-equidistant longitudinal samples in meters. The first
column is `z`, the second is the on-axis longitudinal magnetic field. `OPAL-T`
uses cubic-spline interpolation to resample the data to an equidistant mesh,
then computes Fourier coefficients from that internal mesh.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `AstraMagnetoStatic N_Fourier [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| remaining lines | `z_i [m]`, `Bz_i [T]` |

The appendix explicitly notes that `AstraMagnetoStatic` does not provide a
`FAST` path.

## `1DDynamic`

A `1DDynamic` map is the RF analogue of `1DMagnetoStatic`. An example header is:

```text
1DDynamic 40
-3.0 57.0 4999
1498.953425154
0.0 2.0 199
```

The field is sampled on axis, normalized so that
`max(|E_on axis|) = 1 MV/m`, and evaluated at runtime with the time factor
`cos(omega t + phi)`.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `1DDynamic N_Fourier [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| 2 | `z_start z_end Nz` in cm |
| 3 | frequency in MHz |
| 4 | `r_start r_end Nr` in cm for the optional `FAST` path |
| remaining lines | `Ez` samples in MV/m |

## `AstraDynamic`

`AstraDynamic` accepts a frequency line followed by non-equidistant `z` and
`Ez` samples in meters and MV/m. `OPAL-T` spline-resamples the data to an
internal equidistant mesh before the Fourier reconstruction.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `AstraDynamic N_Fourier [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| 2 | frequency in MHz |
| remaining lines | `z_i [m]`, `Ez_i [MV/m]` |

The appendix again notes that there is no `FAST` variant.

## `1DProfile1`

`1DProfile1` is the special bend-fringe profile format. It uses Enge functions
for the entrance and exit fringe fields [@spencerenge1967],

$$
F(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{\sum_{n=0}^{N_{\mathrm{order}}} c_n (z/D)^n}},
$$ {#eq-fieldmaps-enge-function}

where `D` is the full gap of the magnet and `c_n` are fitted coefficients.
Unlike the other ASCII formats, `1DProfile1` is not normalized to unit peak
field.

The appendix warns that the polynomial degree should be odd and the highest
coefficient should be positive, otherwise the fitted profile may turn upward
again at large distance.

![Polynomial Enge-style profile used for `1DProfile1`.](figures/Enge_poly.png){#fig-fieldmaps-enge width="80%"}

![Profile shape for `1DProfile1`.](figures/profile-1.png){#fig-fieldmaps-profile1 width="80%"}

The generic file layout is:

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `1DProfile1 N_Enge_Entrance N_Enge_Exit Gap` |
| 2 | three entrance parameters plus a placeholder |
| 3 | three exit parameters plus a placeholder |
| following lines | entrance coefficients `c_0 ... c_N` then exit coefficients |

### `1DProfile1` Type 1

Type 1 stores the magnet length implicitly in the difference between the second
exit and entrance parameters. The appendix defines

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Entrance Parameter 1} &= \text{Entrance Parameter 2} - \Delta_1 \\
\text{Entrance Parameter 3} &= \text{Entrance Parameter 2} + \Delta_2 \\
\text{Exit Parameter 2} &= L - \text{Entrance Parameter 2} \\
\text{Exit Parameter 1} &= \text{Exit Parameter 2} - \Delta_3 \\
\text{Exit Parameter 3} &= \text{Exit Parameter 2} + \Delta_4
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-fieldmaps-profile1-type1-input}

and recovers internally

$$
\begin{aligned}
L &= \text{Exit Parameter 2} - \text{Entrance Parameter 2} \\
\Delta_1 &= \text{Entrance Parameter 2} - \text{Entrance Parameter 1} \\
\Delta_2 &= \text{Entrance Parameter 3} - \text{Entrance Parameter 2} \\
\Delta_3 &= \text{Exit Parameter 2} - \text{Exit Parameter 1} \\
\Delta_4 &= \text{Exit Parameter 3} - \text{Exit Parameter 2}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-fieldmaps-profile1-type1-recovered}

![`RBEND` profile geometry for `1DProfile1` type 1.](figures/RBendType1.png){#fig-fieldmaps-rbendtype1 width="60%"}

![`SBEND` profile geometry for `1DProfile1` type 1.](figures/SBendType1.png){#fig-fieldmaps-sbendtype1 width="60%"}

### `1DProfile1` Type 2

Type 2 removes the magnet-length information from the field map and uses the
beamline element attribute `L` instead. This allows the Enge origins to move
relative to the physical edges.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Entrance Parameter 2} &= \text{perpendicular distance of the entrance Enge origin from the entrance edge}, \\
\text{Exit Parameter 2} &= \text{perpendicular distance of the exit Enge origin from the exit edge}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-fieldmaps-profile1-type2-origins}

The remaining deltas are still recovered from the parameter differences. The
two main advantages noted in the appendix are:

- the Enge origins can be adjusted to model the fringe more accurately
- one map can be reused for magnets with identical fringe fields but different
  lengths

## Two-Dimensional Families

### `2DElectroStatic`

Example header:

```text
2DElectroStatic XZ
-3.0 51.0 4999
0.0 2.0 199
0.00000e+00 0.00000e+00
4.36222e-06 0.00000e+00
...
```

This format describes a sampled electrostatic field with bilinear
interpolation. In the legacy workflow these maps were often produced with
Poisson Superfish [@billenyoung2004]. In the source example the map spans `5000` longitudinal points
and `200` radial points. The field is non-negligible from `-3.0 cm` to
`51.0 cm` relative to `ELEMEDGE`, and the radial support is `0.0 cm` to
`2.0 cm`. In `XZ` orientation the first column is `Ez` and the second is `Er`;
for `ZX` orientation the columns are exchanged.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `2DElectroStatic Orientation [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| 2 | fastest-changing axis extent and spacing count |
| 3 | slowest-changing axis extent and spacing count |
| remaining lines | `(Ez, Er)` for `XZ`, `(Er, Ez)` for `ZX` |

### `2DMagnetoStatic`

Example header:

```text
2DMagnetoStatic ZX
0.0 2.0 199
-3.0 51.0 4999
0.00000e+00 0.00000e+00
0.00000e+00 4.36222e-06
...
```

This is the magnetostatic analogue of `2DElectroStatic`. The field is
normalized so that `max(|Bz on axis|) = 1 T`. In the source example the
orientation is `ZX`, so the fastest-changing index is radial and the stored
pair is `(Br, Bz)` rather than `(Bz, Br)`.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `2DMagnetoStatic Orientation [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| 2 | fastest-changing axis extent and spacing count |
| 3 | slowest-changing axis extent and spacing count |
| remaining lines | `(Bz, Br)` for `XZ`, `(Br, Bz)` for `ZX` |

### `2DDynamic`

Example header:

```text
2DDynamic XZ
-3.0 51.0 4121
1498.953425154
0.0 1.0 75
0.00000e+00 0.00000e+00 0.00000e+00 0.00000e+00
...
```

This is the two-dimensional RF format. It adds a frequency line and stores four
values per grid point:

- `Ez`
- `Er`
- `|E|` (present but unused by `OPAL-T`)
- `Hphi`

The first two columns follow the `XZ` / `ZX` orientation rule, while the third
and fourth do not.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `2DDynamic Orientation [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| 2 | fastest-changing axis extent and spacing count |
| 3 | frequency in MHz |
| 4 | slowest-changing axis extent and spacing count |
| remaining lines | `Ez/Er`, `Er/Ez`, `|E|`, `Hphi` |

## Three-Dimensional Families

### `3DMagnetoStatic`

Example header:

```text
3DMagnetoStatic
-1.5 1.5 227
-1.0 1.0 151
-3.0 51.0 4121
0.00e+00 0.00e+00 0.00e+00
...
```

The plain 3D magnetostatic format stores full sampled vector-field data on a
Cartesian grid and uses trilinear interpolation. The legacy ordering is `z`
fastest, then `y`, then `x`. The data columns are `Bx`, `By`, and `Bz`.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `3DMagnetoStatic [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| 2 | `x_start x_end Nx` in cm |
| 3 | `y_start y_end Ny` in cm |
| 4 | `z_start z_end Nz` in cm |
| remaining lines | `Bx By Bz` |

### `3DMagnetoStatic_Extended`

Example header:

```text
3DMagnetoStatic_Extended
-9.9254 9.9254 133
-2.0 1.0 15
-22.425 47.425 465
-8.10970000e-05
...
```

This format stores only a mid-plane magnetic map and reconstructs the 3D field
using Maxwell consistency and a perfect-magnetic-conductor mid-plane symmetry.
The stored quantity is the perpendicular field component on the mid-plane, and
the upper half-plane is mirrored to negative `y`.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `3DMagnetoStatic_Extended [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| 2 | `x_start x_end Nx` in cm |
| 3 | `y_start y_end Ny` in cm |
| 4 | `z_start z_end Nz` in cm |
| remaining lines | stored mid-plane `By` values |

### `3DDynamic`

Example header:

```text
3DDynamic
1498.9534
-1.5 1.5 227
-1.0 1.0 151
-3.0 51.0 4121
0.00e+00 0.00e+00 0.00e+00 0.00e+00 0.00e+00 0.00e+00
...
```

The dynamic 3D format adds a frequency specification and then stores six field
components per sample:

- `Ex`
- `Ey`
- `Ez`
- `Hx`
- `Hy`
- `Hz`

The grid ordering is again `z` fastest, then `y`, then `x`.

| Line | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1 | `3DDynamic [TRUE|FALSE]` |
| 2 | frequency in MHz |
| 3 | `x_start x_end Nx` in cm |
| 4 | `y_start y_end Ny` in cm |
| 5 | `z_start z_end Nz` in cm |
| remaining lines | `Ex Ey Ez Hx Hy Hz` |

::::::
